rows.explanation: It names works, love, faith, service, and patient endurance among the congregation’s qualities.
It describes the saints as keeping God’s commandments, holding faith in Jesus, and showing patience.
It urges believers to stir one another toward love and good works.
It says Abraham’s faith worked together with his deeds and was brought to completion by them.
It tells the community to admonish and encourage one another, help the weak, and be patient with all.
It calls believers to encourage one another as they gather.
It tells believers to exhort one another daily so none is hardened by sin’s deceit.
It says to teach and admonish one another with the word of Christ.
It describes one believer turning another back when that person wanders from the truth.
It says love should be expressed in deed and truth rather than words alone.
It commands people to speak truth with their neighbors as members of one another.
It commands people to speak truth to one another and render truthful, peaceable judgments.
It commands frank rebuke of a neighbor rather than silent complicity in wrongdoing.
It commands preaching, correction, and exhortation with patience and teaching.
It describes believers as able to instruct one another.
It connects patient persistence in doing good with the hope of eternal life.
It describes faith as working through love.
It joins work produced by faith, labor prompted by love, and steadfastness of hope.
It urges imitation of those who inherit the promises through faith and patience.
It says believers should be careful to devote themselves to good works.
It says the righteous shall live by faith.
It joins trusting in the Lord with doing good.
It asserts that no one does good, reversing the ayah’s description of people who do righteous deeds.
It says those who hold fast to the word bear fruit with patience.
It says the disciples were exhorted to continue in the faith and endure tribulations.
It urges persistence in doing good rather than growing weary.
It joins obedience to the truth with fervent love for one another.
It calls believers steadfast and says to abound in the Lord’s work.
It compares the person who hears Jesus’ words and does them to a house that withstands the flood.
It commands people to be doers of the word and not hearers only.
It describes the blameless person as doing righteousness and speaking truth.
It commands people to do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.
It commands people to learn to do good and seek justice.
It says those who turn many to righteousness will shine like the stars.
